title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Opinions on Regulating the Trial Business Relations Between Higher and Lower People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the *Opinions on Regulating the Adjudicative Working Relationship Between Higher and Lower People's Courts*

Fa Fa [2010] No. 61

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The *Opinions on Regulating the Adjudicative Working Relationship Between Higher and Lower People's Courts* of the Supreme People's Court have been adopted at the 1493rd Session of the Adjudicative Committee of the Supreme People's Court. They are hereby issued to you for earnest compliance and implementation in light of the actual adjudicative work.

December 28, 2010

Opinions on Regulating the Adjudicative Working Relationship Between Higher and Lower People's Courts

To further regulate the adjudicative working relationship between higher and lower people's courts, clarify the scope and procedures of supervision and guidance, and ensure that people's courts at all levels independently exercise their adjudicative power in accordance with the law, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the *Constitution of the People's Republic of China*, the *Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China*, and other relevant laws, and in light of actual adjudicative work.

Article 1. The Supreme People's Court shall supervise and guide the adjudicative work of local people's courts at all levels and special people's courts. Higher people's courts shall supervise and guide the adjudicative work of lower people's courts. The scope, methods, and procedures of such supervision and guidance shall comply with legal provisions.

Article 2. People's courts at all levels shall perform their respective duties within the scope prescribed by law and independently exercise their adjudicative power in accordance with the law.

Article 3. For the following types of first-instance cases that have already been accepted, a basic people's court or an intermediate people's court may, when necessary and in accordance with relevant legal provisions, submit a written request to the people's court at the next higher level for adjudication:

(1) Cases of major, difficult, or complex nature;
(2) Cases of a new type;
(3) Cases with significance for the unified application of law;
(4) Cases where the competent people's court is not appropriate to exercise adjudicative power.

Article 4. When a lower people's court requests the transfer of a case for adjudication, the higher people's court shall promptly decide whether to adjudicate the case itself and shall issue a decision granting or denying the transfer request.

Article 5. Where a higher people's court considers that a first-instance case under the jurisdiction of a lower people's court falls within the types listed in Article 3 of these Opinions and it is necessary for the higher people's court to adjudicate the case itself, it may decide to elevate the level of jurisdiction.

Article 6. For cases in which the facts have already been ascertained by the first-instance court, the court of second instance shall, in principle, not remand the case for retrial on the grounds of unclear facts or insufficient evidence.

When the court of second instance renders a ruling to remand the case for retrial, it shall specify in detail the reasons and legal basis for the remand within the ruling.

Article 7. Where the court of second instance remands a case for retrial due to unclear facts or insufficient evidence in the original judgment, it may, in principle, remand the case only once.

Article 8. The Supreme People's Court provides guidance on the adjudicative work of local people's courts at all levels and special people's courts through such means as adjudicating cases, formulating judicial interpretations or normative documents, issuing guiding cases, convening adjudicative work conferences, and organizing judge training.

Article 9. A High People's Court provides guidance on the adjudicative work of people's courts at all levels and special people's courts within its jurisdiction through such means as adjudicating cases, formulating adjudicative work documents, issuing reference cases, convening adjudicative work conferences, and organizing judge training.

Adjudicative work documents formulated by a High People's Court shall be adopted after discussion by its Adjudicative Committee. Where the Supreme People's Court finds that an adjudicative work document formulated by a High People's Court conflicts with current laws or judicial interpretations, it shall order the High People's Court to correct the document.

Article 10. An Intermediate People's Court provides guidance on the adjudicative work of basic people's courts through such means as adjudicating cases, summarizing adjudicative experience, and organizing judge training.

Article 11. These Opinions shall come into effect on the date of promulgation.
